title: Parallelized re-scorer pipeline with per-request token budgets and soft timeouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: The re-scoring/ordering endpoint is a major contributor to tail latency in downstream search and recommendation flows. Current behavior serially scores candidate sets (or uses coarse microbatches) with a single hard token cap and synchronous KV cache fetches. As candidate counts and token variance grow, p95/p99 latency and cost are both increasing.
goals: Reduce p95 endpoint latency for 32-candidate median workloads by >=25% under steady-state load
Provide per-request configurable token budgets so high-priority requests can get more compute without starving bulk inference
Implement a graceful early-exit (soft timeout) that returns best-available scores instead of failing or waiting for full token budgets
Preserve or improve end-to-end ranking quality (no >1% relative drop in NDCG@10 on eval prompts)
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for canonical rerank scenario drops from baseline ~220ms to <=165ms on runtime-1.22 with default config
Support per-request header X-Token-Budget and X-Latency-SLO with sane defaults; documented in API spec
Soft timeout returns deterministic partial scoring with a confidence field for consumer fallback logic
End-to-end eval run (10k prompts) shows <=1% NDCG@10 regression compared to current production model
No increase in 99th-percentile GPU utilization that would cause capacity violations under the regression test harness
design_notes: Parallelization: switch to a per-candidate worker pool with cooperative scheduling. Each worker executes up to 'token_budget_per_candidate' tokens but yields between candidates to allow time-aware fairness.
Token budgets: support three budget modes - fixed (legacy), proportional (budget distributed by candidate length estimate), and priority-weighted (honors X-Token-Budget header).

Soft timeouts: implement deadline watcher that triggers an orderly truncation of in-flight candidates, returning partial logits/scores and a 'soft_exit' boolean and 'confidence_est' metric. This avoids hard failures on overloaded paths.
KV prefetch: prefetch keys for top-K candidates in a lightweight speculative pass. Prefetch is amortized and piggybacks on candidate metadata to avoid stall on first attention calls.

Microbatching: replace rigid microbatch sizes with adaptive 'time-bucket' slicing. The scheduler collects candidates for a short window (configurable, e.g., 3-5ms) then forms batches prioritized by deadline and budget. This reduces jitter while keeping latency bounds.

Backpressure: add an admission controller that rejects or demotes low-priority bulk requests when the worker queue exceeds a high-water mark. Responses include Retry-After and reason codes for consumer logic.

Metrics: emit candidate-level timing (kv_fetch_ms, model_compute_ms, score_finalize_ms), soft_exit_rate, budget_overrides, and per-request token_consumed. Add a dashboard with p50/p95/p99 breakdown by candidate count and token variance.

Quality tradeoff: conservative defaults favor quality (larger budgets) but system exposes knobs to reduce token budgets aggressively for cost-sensitive tiers. We will run A/B on a shadow fleet before enabling aggressive defaults.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Scheduler & API - add X-Token-Budget / X-Latency-SLO headers and internal deadline propagation (ENG-41621-sched-api PR).
Phase 2: Worker pool - implement cooperative per-candidate workers and time-bucket microbatching. Add unit tests for scheduler fairness and preemption.
Phase 3: KV prefetch - implement speculative prefetch pass and measure marginal fetch latency reduction (ENG-41234 referenced).
Phase 4: Soft timeout logic - implement deterministic partial scoring contract and add consumer-facing confidence field; update client SDKs to handle soft exits.
Phase 5: Dogfood and canary - route 5% traffic to optimized path in canary; collect metrics and run quality eval harness; iterate on budget heuristics.
Phase 6: Rollout - staged ramp and rollback knobs; finalize docs and SDK examples.
test_plan: Unit tests: scheduler fairness, token budget arithmetic, deadline propagation, KV prefetch mock timings.
Integration: end-to-end test harness simulating 8/16/32 candidate workloads with token length variance; assert latency targets and stable scoring outputs.
Load: run scaled load test against runtime-1.22 in perf cluster; measure GPU utilization, p95/p99, and soft_exit_rate under overload scenarios.
Quality regression: run 10k eval prompts against production model and compare NDCG@10, MRR; run human spot checks for edge cases.
Chaos: introduce artificial KV delays to confirm graceful degradation and no cascading failures.
rollout_plan: Canary 5%: enable path for internal tenants + dev customers. Observe soft_exit_rate and user-visible latency for 72h.
Ramp 25%: expand to non-critical customers after addressing any regressions.
Ramp 100%: full rollout after 7 days of stable metrics and signoff from SRE and PM.
Rollback: immediate toggle to legacy scheduler and token handling if soft_exit_rate > 2% or p95 regresses by >10%.
Postmortem: capture learnings and update runbooks for soft exits and consumer SDK guidance.
